title: Dod, or, har: d, r, e, u
topic: ד ר; the vowels e (tsere, segol) and u (shuruk, kubutz)
why: Two letters (ד and ר) and the last two vowels, e and u: you can now read all the basic vowels. You also discover the three uses of ו and job words in the masculine and the feminine.

{"lessons": ["

Two new letters: ד and ר

LetterNameSound
דdaletd
רreshr, from the back of the throat, like the French r (not the English r)

Look closely at the shape: ד has a sharp corner at the top right, ר is completely rounded. With them, you can finally read תּוֹדָה and מְאוֹד without help.

דּוֹדdod: uncle
הַרhar: mountain

The dot in דּ (the dagesh) changes nothing: דּ and ד are always read d. Only a few letters change their sound with the dot, like בּ (b) and ב (v).

", "

The vowel e: two marks

MarkSoundExample
נֵ (two dots side by side: tsere)eנֵר ner, candle
דֶ (three dots in a triangle: segol)eדֶּלֶת delet, door

In modern Hebrew, both marks are read the same way: an e as in \"bed\", never \"ee\". There is never a silent e: every e is pronounced, דֶּלֶת = de-let.

יֶלֶד / יַלְדָּהyeled / yalda: a boy / a girl (a child)
תֵּל אָבִיבTel Aviv

Job words have one form for a man and one for a woman, often with a final a in the feminine: מוֹרֶה (more), מוֹרָה (mora), teacher; תַּלְמִיד (talmid), תַּלְמִידָה (talmida), student.

", "

The vowel u and the three lives of ו

The sound \"u\" (like the oo in food) is written in two ways: a vav with a dot in the middle, וּ (shuruk), as in רוּת (Rut, Ruth), or three slanted dots under the letter (kubutz), as in בֻּבָּה (buba, doll).

SpellingSoundExample
ו + a vowelvדָּוִד David
וֹoאוֹר or, light
וּu (oo)רוּת Rut
וְ attached to the next wordve: andאַבָּא וְאִמָּא dad and mom
הוּא מוֹרֶה, הִיא תַּלְמִידָה.He is a teacher, she is a student. [hu more, hi talmida]

Before ב or מ, \"and\" is pronounced u and written וּ: וּמִי? (u-mi?), and who?
